content:
sam: Heads-up — I'm kicking off a short sprint to rewrite the fragmentation surface for heterogeneous memory (GPU/host). Goal is to make eviction/compaction reasoning explicit and easier to instrument.

ravi: +1. Want to make sure we don't accidentally blow the hot-path with extra checks.

angela: Curious what the proposed interface looks like. Are we talking new allocator APIs or just adapter layers?

sam: Thinking layered. Minimal allocator API changes (few exported hints) and a new "frag-coordinator" module that owns long-running compaction jobs, heuristics, and telemetry. Allocator stays fast for alloc/free; coordinator does the heavy work async.

mike: Sounds good. Can you enumerate the hints? e.g., "can_compact", "pin_till_idle", "evict_priority"?

sam: Exactly. Draft hints:
- can_compact: boolean — candidate for compaction
- eviction_weight: int (0-100) — tenant fairness hint
- hot_score_bucket: string — quick hot/cold classification
- pin_handle: token if caller wants longer residency

tara: Will those be per-allocation or per-arena? per-allocation seems heavy.

sam: Per-allocation metadata but stored compactly in slab headers; arenas can override defaults. We avoid touching the critical path often — writes to headers are atomic and cheap.

angela: How do we handle mixed-size fragments that cross slab boundaries? This is where fragmentation gets nasty.

ravi: Proposal: coordinator works with a "recluster" phase that gathers relocation candidates across slabs, builds moveops, then applies them when busier lanes are free. Move ops are page-aligned to avoid partial mappings.

mike: So we need a cross-arena lockless staging queue for moveops? That sounds like potential contention.

sam: We'll use per-arena staging queues and a global scheduler that steals work. Staging entries are compact (ptr + length + hint). Apply phase uses epoch-based safety so allocators can proceed without heavy locking.

angela: Epoch safety + async moves — nice. What's the fallback if a move fails (OOM on target, or CPU->GPU transfer error)?

sam: Fallbacks: retry with backoff; if still fails, mark candidate as "demote" (prefer host-backed) and emit telemetry. Critical to avoid dropping allocations; we'll prefer demotion over abort.

tara: Telemetry items we want: pre/post fragmentation heatmap, move success rate, time-to-finalize for a recluster job, eviction ratios.

ciara-bot: deploybot: scheduled an experiment namespace for canary runs: infra-sprint-frag-01, retention 7d.

ravi: For the canary, what's the perf target? We should define acceptable regressions.

sam: Targets: 1) no more than 2% tail-latency increase at p99 for small-batch inferences; 2) at least 10% reduction in cold-start evictions in mixed workloads; 3) no disk spill increase >5%.

mike: How do we measure "cold-start evictions"? Need a metric definition for alerts.

tara: Suggest metric: "evictions_per_cold_session" where a session is defined by first request timestamp -> 5m. Count evicts triggered for allocations that were created in that window.

angela: Backwards compatibility: older private deployments might not have coordinator enabled. Need a safe opt-in via runtime flag and default off for >= Major2 releases?

sam: Yes opt-in. We'll add feature flag runtime.enable_frag_coordinator. Default off for existing clusters, on for canary infra. Coordinator will degrade to noop if not enabled.

ravi: API surface for SDKs? Customers may rely on pinning semantics. Do we expose new hints in public SDK or keep internal-only for now?

sam: Internal-only first. After a couple canary cycles and API stability review, we can offer a "pin_handle" binding in the SDK with strong docs.

mike: One more: compaction vs compact-on-write tradeoff. Do we do proactive compact-on-write (compact small holes when writing) or background recluster?

sam: Hybrid: compact-on-write for micro-frag cases (cheap local coalesces), recluster for macro-frag (cross-slab). Coordinator will decide based on fragmentation window and cost model.

angela: Cost model inputs? bandwidth cost, GPU memcpy cost, predicted reuse (hot_score), and tenant SLA weight.

ravi: We'll need a simulator to tune thresholds. Can we reuse the old frag-sim harness and add heterogeneous transfer costs?

sam: Yes reuse and extend. I'll put up a PR adding GPU memcpy latencies per instance type.

tara: Timeline for sprint?

sam: Plan: Day 0-2 design freeze + review; Day 3-7 implement coordinator skeleton + hints; Day 8-12 integrate recluster logic and epoch safety; Day 13-15 smoke tests + canary deploy.

mike: Can I own the epoch-safety bits and staging queues?

sam: Please. @mike owning epoch-safety. @ravi and @angela pair on recluster heuristics. @tara on telemetry. I'll coordinate the PRs and canary.

angela: One question for later: do we need to version slab header layout? If so, how to migrate?

sam: We avoid breaking layout — store the new hint index in a per-arena side-table if we need to extend metadata later. Avoid header churn.

ravi: OK. I'll help with the side-table impl.

tara: I'll draft the metrics dashboard tiles and alert thresholds after first canary run.

sam: Sweet. I'll post the design doc link in a follow-up with diagrams and the proto for hints. Thanks all. :rocket:
